chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Muslims are bound by their conditions, except every condition that contravenes the Book of Allah, Mighty and Exalted; then it is not permissible.

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُونَ: the Muslims; the community addressed as legally bound by valid agreements
key_terms.شُرُوطِهِمْ: their conditions; stipulated terms in agreements and transactions
key_terms.فَلَا يَجُوزُ: then it is not permissible; it has no lawful validity
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah; the divine scriptural standard by which conditions are judged

ai.seo_question: Are Muslims required to fulfill contractual conditions if those conditions contradict the Book of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a foundational legal principle that agreements and stipulated conditions are binding among Muslims. However, any condition that conflicts with the Book of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has no legal validity and is not permissible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3765 - Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) who said:
"Muslims are bound by their conditions, except for any condition that contradicts the Book of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, which is not permissible."
